clue.text: Bad actor will scoff at swing for relaxation

parts.note: a ham is a hammy, over-the-top performer
to mock is to scoff at or deride

explanation.surface: A poor performer is going to sneer at a playground swing meant for unwinding.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammock is a hanging bed of netting or canvas that sways, used for lounging in gardens.

clue.text: Do "Bill greeting woman"

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill to be paid
hi is a casual greeting
Eve, the first woman in Genesis, stands for any woman

explanation.surface: An instruction to perform a sketch called 'Bill greeting woman'.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Do' look like 'perform this'; it is the definition, as in 'do what you set out to do'.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something, in the sense of carrying it out successfully, is to accomplish or bring it about.

clue.text: Greek character extraordinarily fit for a civilian

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: something done extraordinarily is out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek man unusually well suited to life outside the forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinarily' rearranges the letters of the clue word fit. Mufti is plain clothes worn by someone off duty, the dress of a civilian; 'for a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mufti is ordinary clothing worn by service personnel off duty, i.e. civilian dress as opposed to uniform.

clue.text: Made like a loco, very pleased

definitions.meaning: a steam locomotive puffs, giving out short bursts of steam and noise
British slang for delighted with oneself

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a steam engine puffing along, and the British colloquial sense of being delighted.

clue.text: Take hold of couple following me around

indicators.note: the couple comes after the turned-round me
turned around, so the word me is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a brace is a pair, as of game birds

explanation.surface: Grab a pair who are trailing behind me as I go about.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace someone is to clasp or take hold of them in one's arms.

clue.text: Sufferer from public transport going over unknown runs

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle of public transport
y is an algebraic unknown
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A victim of a bus or tram that ploughs over an unidentified jogger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' turns TRAM to MART.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyr is one who suffers or dies for a cause, hence a sufferer generally.

clue.text: Close to new technology in scripture lesson, continuing the performance

indicators.note: the close and the technology are placed inside the lesson's letters

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, the old school name for scripture lessons
a close is an end or conclusion
IT, information technology, is the newer technology
on means continuing, as in 'carry on'

explanation.surface: Bringing modern gadgets into a Bible class nearly done, keeping the show going.
explanation.walkthrough: RI (religious instruction) was the British school subject now usually called RE. 'to' simply joins END and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is a performance or interpretation of a piece of music or drama.

clue.text: Conspire with Sebastian to hold up pedestrian

indicators.note: Coe's letters hold the other piece inside them

parts.note: Sebastian Coe, the British Olympic middle-distance runner

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: pedestrian in the sense of dull, uninspired

explanation.surface: Plotting with a famous runner to delay a walker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' and 'up' work together: the runner's surname holds the upturned synonym. 'Pedestrian' looks like a walker, but means uninspired.
explanation.definitionFit: To collude is to act secretly together, i.e. to conspire with others.

clue.text: Little fastener for unruly wig left down by tree

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
a pin fastens things together

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: low and down both mean dejected

explanation.surface: A small clip to keep a messy hairpiece in place, abandoned near a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges WIG to GWI. 'for' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The weeping willow is a willow tree with long drooping branches.

clue.text: Quiche failure largely down to head of kitchen

indicators.note: the answer is carried within the larger run of letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A ruined quiche is mostly the fault of the person in charge of the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across quiCHE Failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Chef comes from French chef de cuisine, literally the head of the kitchen.

clue.text: Never putting a foot wrong under heartless king, lying glibly

indicators.note: without its heart, so the central letter of under is removed

parts.note: taken as written
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: done glibly, carelessly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Faultless, beneath a cruel monarch, by telling smooth lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the D from UNDER to leave UNER; 'glibly' rearranges LYING into INGLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Unerringly means without ever making a mistake, always accurate.

clue.text: Faith, old dear — live first!

indicators.note: the word for live comes before the other piece

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
lief is an archaic word meaning dear or beloved

explanation.surface: An elderly lady's motto: live life first, faith comes after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old dear' looks like an elderly woman; it means the archaic word for dear.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief is faith, especially trust in a religion or creed.

clue.text: Awfully shy, taking umbrage about figure

indicators.note: the umbrage word goes around the shuffled letters

parts.note: pique is resentment, as is umbrage

indicators.note: awfully suggests badly done, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A very bashful person taking offence about their body shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' jumbles the clue word shy, and 'about' puts the umbrage word around it; 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Physique is one's bodily build or shape, one's figure.

clue.text: Death may result in shortage of cash for drug

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged to give a new outcome
money falls short by its last letter

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: Lack of funds can lead to a fatal outcome, for an addict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortage of' cuts MONEY to MONE, and 'may result in' rearranges DEATH with MONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Methadone is a synthetic opioid drug, used as a substitute in treating heroin addiction.

clue.text: Shrill companion takes the strain for raising the young

parts.note: a shrill sound is high-pitched
CH is Companion of Honour, a British honour
an air or strain is a tune

explanation.surface: A piercing-voiced partner bears the burden of bringing up children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like stress, but is a musical strain, an air. 'Raising' is both rearing and literally lifting the infant up to table height.
explanation.definitionFit: A highchair is a tall chair for an infant, lifting a small child up to feed at table.

clue.text: Tear apart, given time to bolt

parts.note: rive is an old word meaning to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: Rip something open, then be given a moment to run off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolt' looks like run off; it is a metal fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivet is a metal pin or bolt used for fastening plates together.

clue.text: Pretend soldier's back in the bog

indicators.note: the turned soldier goes into the bog word

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land, a bog

indicators.note: back means the soldier word is read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier; the 's is no letter

explanation.surface: A trooper pretends to be stuck in a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the American soldier, and 'in' places him in the marsh; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign is to pretend or simulate.

clue.text: Learned to diet, rue conniving

indicators.note: conniving means scheming, so these letters are rearranged deviously

explanation.surface: Someone taught themselves to go on a diet, then regretted plotting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective, pronounced as two syllables.
explanation.definitionFit: An erudite person is learned, having great knowledge from study.

clue.text: The distance covered by pigs takes son a second to achieve with rapidity

indicators.note: the distance unit sits within the pigs word

parts.note: swine are pigs
FT, feet, is a measure of distance

explanation.surface: How far pigs travel takes a boy a moment to achieve at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' puts the feet inside the pigs; 'takes', 'a' and 'to achieve' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiftness means speed, the quality of being fast, which is rapidity.

clue.text: Good pieces in seemly fabrication

indicators.note: the good and the pieces go inside the seemly word

parts.note: fit means proper or seemly
chessmen are pieces, so men

explanation.surface: Fine bits of something proper turn out to be made up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' looks like bits, but means chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A figment is something invented or made up, a fabrication of the imagination.

clue.text: The kind of Constable that's out of the ordinary

definitions.meaning: a part-time volunteer British police officer is a ... Constable

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the word: a British volunteer police officer, and the ordinary sense of exceptional.

clue.text: Boss circulates, sanctimonious, thick

indicators.note: the boss word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised ornamental knob
pi is slang for piously self-righteous

explanation.surface: A preachy manager walking around the office is dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager; it is a knob or stud.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick is informal for slow-witted or dull, i.e. stupid.

clue.text: Must lace trifle with wine

indicators.note: to trifle with something is to mess about with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trifle has to be spiked with some sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' looks like the pudding but is the verb to play about with.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscatel is a sweet wine made from muscat grapes.

clue.text: Drinking vessel in our country is nothing to the French model

indicators.note: the nothing goes inside the country's letters

parts.note: GB, Great Britain, is the setter's home country
O looks like zero, nothing
le is the masculine French word for the
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: In Britain, a cup is worthless next to a French design.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet is a drinking glass or cup with a foot and stem.

clue.text: Sounds of disapprobation for the drink

indicators.note: sounds means the word is said aloud

parts.note: boos are calls of disapproval

explanation.surface: Jeers greet the alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is informal for alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Don't hold with careless vapid prose

indicators.note: careless suggests sloppy arrangement, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A critic objects to slapdash, empty writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To not hold with something is to object to it or think it wrong.

clue.text: Norse god is full of good intentions

indicators.note: the answer is contained within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian deity means well.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across goOD INtentions.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief of the gods in Norse mythology.

clue.text: Caesar's words to Brutus turned the lines completely

indicators.note: turned round, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: et tu, Brute were Caesar's dying words to Brutus in Shakespeare
RLY is short for railway, the lines

explanation.surface: Caesar's reproach to Brutus completely changed the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes ET TU into UTTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly means totally, to the full degree, i.e. completely.
